questions.explanation: Amylase is a carbohydrase enzyme that breaks down starch into the disaccharide maltose. It is produced in the salivary glands, pancreas, and small intestine.

questions.stem: Where is pepsin produced and what is its optimum pH?
questions.explanation: Pepsin is a protease enzyme produced by the stomach lining. It works best at around pH 2, the acidic conditions created by hydrochloric acid in the stomach.
Lipase is the enzyme that breaks down fats (lipids) into fatty acids and glycerol. It is produced mainly by the pancreas and works in the small intestine.

questions.stem: Why does the pancreas produce sodium bicarbonate along with its enzymes?

options.text: To neutralise stomach acid and provide the alkaline pH needed for intestinal enzymes
To make the food taste better

questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate neutralises the acidic chyme from the stomach, creating the slightly alkaline conditions (pH 7-8) needed for pancreatic enzymes to work at their optimum pH.

options.text: Breaks down maltose into two glucose molecules
Breaks down fat into fatty acids
Breaks down protein into amino acids

questions.explanation: Maltase is produced in the lining of the small intestine and breaks down the disaccharide maltose into two glucose molecules, which can then be absorbed.

questions.stem: Why can't pepsin work in the small intestine?

options.text: There is no food in the small intestine
The alkaline pH of the small intestine denatures pepsin

questions.explanation: Pepsin has an optimum pH of about 2. The alkaline conditions in the small intestine (pH 7-8) denature pepsin, changing the shape of its active site so it can no longer function.

questions.stem: How does bile help lipase work more effectively?

options.text: Bile removes lipase from the system
Bile emulsifies fats into smaller droplets, increasing the surface area for lipase to act on
Bile is a type of lipase

questions.explanation: Bile emulsifies fats, breaking large fat globules into smaller droplets. This increases the total surface area of fat exposed to lipase, allowing it to digest the fat more quickly.
